original_question: For the Z_k-equivariant differential equations z' = iz + (z zbar)^n zbar^{k+1} with positive integers n and k, is the period function of the period annulus at the origin monotonically decreasing?
target_in_paper: Problem 16 in Section 3.5, "Some reversible equivariant planar differential systems," asking whether the period function of the center at the origin for equation (15) is monotonously decreasing. This problem is posed immediately after Proposition 3.1, which gives the paper’s precise reduction to a subfamily of reversible quadratic centers. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2012.02524))
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the intended topic: the open monotonicity problem for the period function of the period annulus of the origin in the paper’s Z_k-equivariant family, with quantification over positive integers n and k. That is the substance of Problem 16. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2012.02524))
missing_details: The differential equation is misstated in your draft: in the paper, equation (15) is dz/dt = i z + (z\bar z)^n z^{k+1}, not dz/dt = i z + (z\bar z)^n \bar z^{k+1}. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2012.02524))

The paper formulates the problem for a planar polynomial differential equation written in complex coordinates z in C (equivalently R^2), and explicitly as a Z_k-equivariant family. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2012.02524))

Equation (15) is introduced for n in N and k > 0, but Problem 16 itself restricts to positive integers n and k; the n = 0 case is excluded there because the paper separately notes that it is holomorphic and hence has an isochronous center. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2012.02524))

To make the question fully stand-alone, it should say that the origin is a reversible center, so that the period annulus of the origin and its period function are the relevant objects. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2012.02524))

The nearby exact reformulation supplied by the paper is missing from the draft: Proposition 3.1 shows that the behaviour and number of critical periods coincide with those of the quadratic reversible center dx/dt = -y + xy, dy/dt = x + D x^2 + F y^2, with F = 1 + D and D = -k/(2(k+n)). ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2012.02524))

If one wants the family described intrinsically, the nonlinear term is homogeneous of total degree 2n + k + 1 in the real planar variables. This is implicit in equation (15) but not stated in your draft. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2012.02524))

No extra nilpotency, degeneracy, or asymptotic qualifier appears in the paper’s formulation; the only hypotheses are that the system belongs to this explicit Z_k-equivariant family and that n,k are positive integers. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2012.02524))
refined_question: For every pair of positive integers n and k, consider the planar polynomial Z_k-equivariant differential equation written in complex form dz/dt = i z + (z\bar z)^n z^{k+1}, where z in C and the origin is its reversible center. Is the period function associated to the period annulus of the origin monotonically decreasing? ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2012.02524))
equivalent_formulation: By Proposition 3.1, this is equivalent to asking: for each positive-integer pair (n,k), does the reversible quadratic center dx/dt = -y + xy, dy/dt = x + D x^2 + F y^2, with F = 1 + D and D = -k/(2(k+n)) in (-1/2,0), have a monotonically decreasing period function at the origin? ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2012.02524))
justification: The draft is clearly targeting Problem 16, not the broader Chicone/Loud problem of Problem 15, because it asks about the specific Z_k-equivariant family (15). The closest paper-faithful sharpening is therefore to restate Problem 16 with the exact equation, ambient variable, and quantifiers, and to record the paper’s own equivalent quadratic-center reformulation from Proposition 3.1. The main substantive correction is replacing \bar z^{k+1} by z^{k+1}. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2012.02524))
